pipeline_mapping: d29 opening anchor: the three asteroid products with an in-space use are volatiles, free metals and bulk dirt; ordinary-chondrite metal can be processed to very pure Fe and Ni for structures in LEO with Co, PGMs, Ga, Ge and As as byproducts; iron meteorites have crushing strengths up to 3600 bar and iron asteroids pose significant processing challenges. Backs the role (not the value) of the structural rows (Fe, Ni, Co, nickel-iron, awaruite 0.70) and of bulk dirt as LEO shielding (d28 silicate rows); C1 chondrites carry up to 20% water, 6% organics, 11% magnetite (d30 rows)

pipeline_mapping: d29: the state of the plant that turns raw metal into parts. NASA's on-demand metals manufacturing project was cancelled before flight; its FabLab sintering furnace drew about 2250 W against a 2000 W target; feedstock from in-situ resources is the last (infusion) phase of the plan. Supports the in-space manufacturing gap behind the structural 0.70 and the geo 0.15 in IN_SPACE_UTILITY (judgement rows); ISS spares of 13,000 kg prepositioned plus 18,000 kg premanufactured (as cited) are context for d15 demand
